deities: Mata Tripurmalini (Goddess Durga; the temple is counted among the 51 Shakti Peethas - the site where Sati's right breast is believed to have fallen)
Kali (shrine adjacent to the main sanctum)
Lord Shiva (large seated statue in the centre of the talab, water spouting like a fountain)
Shiva lingam in the replica Amarnath Cave, plus figurines and paintings of many Hindu deities
festivals: Shri Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan (annual classical music festival in December; one of India's oldest, established 1875; Ravi Shankar performed here in 1977)

Content mirrors that entry: the 51-Shakti-Peetha shrine to Mata Tripurmalini on Tanda Road, Jalandhar, whose focal point is a large talab ringed by a broad causeway with a seated Shiva statue in the centre spouting water like a fountain; the complex includes an adjacent Kali shrine, a replica Amarnath Cave with a Shiva lingam, and a mock mountain. name: Devi Talab Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, with roots reaching the ancient period and a name tied in legend to the demon Jalandhara; it is a major Doaba-region commercial and industrial centre on NH-44. The Devi Talab Mandir on Tanda Road, about 1 km from the railway station, is the city's most famous Shakti shrine and a 51-Shakti-Peetha site. It anchors one of the oldest religious quarters of the city.

travel.airport: Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport, Amritsar (~80 km); Adampur domestic airport is closer (~25 km, limited service - verify).
travel.railway: Jalandhar City Junction on the Delhi-Amritsar line, about 1 km from the temple.
travel.road: On NH-44; well connected to Amritsar (80 km), Ludhiana (60 km) and Delhi (375 km). The temple is on Tanda Road, reached by auto/taxi.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; December for the Harballabh Sangeet Sammelan; Navratri for festivals.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as open daily 5:00 AM to 10:00 PM (verify - per devitalabmandir.com listing). Free entry.
